newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto said off on amortization concerns.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto said off on amortization concerns.

text.p: Monsanto Co shares traded down 1-1/4 at 37-1/4 on concerns that St. Louis-based company could face increased amortization in 1997 related to its planned acquisition of Holden's Foundation Seed Co, analysts said.
"There is a concern that with the Holden's acquisition, some of that (cost) has to be amortized over a certain number of years," Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said.
She added Monsanto may reap a tax advantage for taking as much of the expected Holden's amortization as possible in the near-term, which could hurt earnings.
Weakness in the stock market also hurt Monsanto shares, analysts added.

Monsanto said earlier this month it plans to buy Holden's as well as Corn States Hybrid Service and Corn States International for about $1.0 billion. It said at the time the deal could dilute earnings for two or three years.

Merrill Lynch analyst Doug Groh added that Monsanto could see a decline in its future profit margins as it focuses more on agricultural and pharmaceutical operations that typically have increased development costs. Monsanto plans to spin off its chemical operations.
"That likely will reduce margins, at least initially," Groh said. "So the great margins that Monsanto had enjoyed are going to be somewhat diminished."
Wittenburg rates Monsanto a buy based on long-term growth potential. Groh has a long-term buy on the stock.
Earlier, Monsanto reported a fourth quarter loss of $0.69 a share, after an $0.84 charge, compared with year-ago earnings of $0.13, which included a $0.02 charge.
For the year, its adjusted earnings were $1.50 a share, up from $1.25 a year ago, excluding extraordinaries in both periods. These results were in line with expectations.
